summary.title: Environmentally friendly and roll-processed flexible organic solar cells based on PM6:Y6
summary.authors: Marcial Fernández Castro, Jean Truer, Espíndola Rodríguez, Jens Wenzel
summary.executive_summary: This study addresses the 'lab-to-fab gap' in Organic Solar Cells (OSCs) by demonstrating the fabrication of flexible, high-efficiency devices using scalable slot-die coating techniques. While lab-scale efficiencies for PM6:Y6 systems exceed 15%, industrial-compatible processes have historically lagged due to material waste and poor upscaling potential of spin-coating. The authors utilize a green solvent, o-xylene, without additives, to coat the PM6:Y6 active layer on flexible ITO/PET substrates. A key challenge, the temperature-dependent aggregation (TDA) of PM6, is managed via a heated slot-die process where the substrate, syringe, tube, and head are maintained at the same temperature. The study systematically optimizes coating temperature (60-120 °C) and solution concentration (12-28 mg/mL). Results indicate that 100 °C is the optimal coating temperature, balancing improved carrier collection (higher JSC) against fill factor losses caused by edge aggregation at higher temperatures. The optimal active layer thickness is found to be approximately 217 nm (24 mg/mL), yielding a binary device efficiency of 6.3%. Furthermore, the introduction of a small amount of PC61BM as a third component enhances performance, achieving a champion efficiency of 7.2% and an average of 6.7%. Photophysical analysis reveals that the ternary blend improves exciton dissociation and charge collection probabilities. Stability tests under dark storage show minimal degradation, with ternary devices retaining 99.4% of initial efficiency after 1050 hours. This work demonstrates that high-efficiency, environmentally friendly OSCs can be manufactured using roll-compatible processes, paving the way for commercialization.

claims.description: Slot-die coating of PM6:Y6 on flexible substrates is feasible using green solvents.
Ternary blends with PCBM improve efficiency and stability.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study addresses the 'lab-to-fab gap' in Organic Solar Cells (OSCs) by demonstrating the fabrication of flexible, high-efficiency devices using scalable slot-die coating techniques. While lab-scale efficiencies for PM6:Y6 systems exceed 15%, industrial-compatible processes have historically lagged due to material waste and poor upscaling potential of spin-coating. The authors utilize a green solvent, o-xylene, without additives, to coat the PM6:Y6 active layer on flexible ITO/PET substrates. A key challenge, the temperature-dependent aggregation (TDA) of PM6, is managed via a heated slot-die process where the substrate, syringe, tube, and head are maintained at the same temperature. The study systematically optimizes coating temperature (60-120 °C) and solution concentration (12-28 mg/mL). Results indicate that 100 °C is the optimal coating temperature, balancing improved carrier collection (higher JSC) against fill factor losses caused by edge aggregation at higher temperatures. The optimal active layer thickness is found to be approximately 217 nm (24 mg/mL), yielding a binary device efficiency of 6.3%. Furthermore, the introduction of a small amount of PC61BM as a third component enhances performance, achieving a champion efficiency of 7.2% and an average of 6.7%. Photophysical analysis reveals that the ternary blend improves exciton dissociation and charge collection probabilities. Stability tests under dark storage show minimal degradation, with ternary devices retaining 99.4% of initial efficiency after 1050 hours. This work demonstrates that high-efficiency, environmentally friendly OSCs can be manufactured using roll-compatible processes, paving the way for commercialization.

Research Context
Organic Solar Cells have reached high efficiencies using lab-scale manufacturing. This creates a significant 'lab-to-fab gap' challenge for competitiveness. Spin-coating is common but has poor potential for upscaling. Slot-die coating is preferred for roll-to-roll manufacturing. Few studies report solar cells using these scalable techniques. Environmentally friendly upscaling requires non-hazardous solvent systems. PM6:Y6 systems show excellent efficiencies over 15% on rigid substrates. There is a need to transfer PM6:Y6 to roll-processing.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to minimize the lab-to-fab gap using scalable techniques. The central question is whether high-efficiency PM6:Y6 cells can be slot-die coated. The hypothesis is that hot slot-die coating can manage PM6 aggregation. It is predicted that optimizing temperature and thickness will maximize PCE. The study hypothesizes that adding PCBM will improve charge transport. The goal is to achieve high efficiencies on flexible substrates. The authors expect to contribute to reducing the lab-to-fab gap.

Methodological Details
The active layer materials PM6 and Y6 were purchased from 1-Material Inc. The flexible substrate is pre-patterned ITO-coated polyethylene terephthalate (PET). The solvent used was o-xylene with purity greater than 98%. The device geometry is inverted: ITO/ZnO/PM6:Y6/MoO3/Ag. A homemade roll-coater was used for slot-die coating. The ZnO ETL was coated at 75 °C and annealed at 100 °C. The PM6:Y6 active layer was coated at temperatures from 60 to 120 °C. Solution concentrations ranged from 12 to 28 mg/mL. The drum speed was kept at 1.5 m/min. The flow rate for the active layer was 0.12 mL/min. MoO3 and Ag were thermally evaporated under vacuum. The base pressure during evaporation was 2 x 10^-5 mbar. The approximate active area of the devices is 0.8 cm^2. J-V curves were measured with a Keithley 2400 source meter. The aperture area was defined as 0.3996 cm^2 using a shadow mask. EQE measurements were performed from 300 to 1100 nm.

Procedures And Architectures
The slot-die head, syringe, drum, and tube were heated. This heating ensures the ink remains liquid during coating. An activation process involves a reverse bias current of -5 V. The maximum current during activation is 100 mA. Encapsulation uses epoxy-based glue EPXR. Curing is done under UV light for approximately 5 minutes. The curing temperature reaches 66 ± 0.5 °C. Thickness measurements were done with a DS95-50 AFM. The scan dimension for AFM is 5 × 5 µm^2. The non-contact mode was used for AFM scans. Light intensity was varied from 62.14 to 147.33 mW/cm^2. The solar simulator was calibrated to 1000 W/m^2. A monocrystalline silicon reference cell was used for calibration. The deposition rate was monitored with an INFICON XTM/2 system.

Key Results
The optimal coating temperature was found to be 100 °C. At 100 °C, the average PCE is slightly higher than at 120 °C. The average FF at 120 °C is 42.2%, lower than at 100 °C. The average FF at 100 °C is 47.10%. The S value for bimolecular recombination at 100 °C is 0.978. The optimal active layer thickness is 217 nm. The highest PCE in thickness optimization is 6.3%. The FF for the 217 nm device is 49.0%. The average PCE for the 217 nm thickness is 5.8%. The S value for the 217 nm device is 0.987. The ternary device with [1:1:0.2] ratio achieved a champion PCE of 7.2%. The average PCE of the [1:1:0.2] ternary device is 6.6%. The average PCE of the [1:1.1:0.1] ternary device is 6.7%. The average FF for [1:1.1:0.1] is 49.1%. The average FF for [1:1:0.2] is 47.3%. The JSC for ternary devices reaches up to 20 mA/cm^2. The dissociation probability for the binary device is 93.7%. The dissociation probability for the [1:1:0.2] ternary device is 96.3%. The collection probability for the binary device is 69.6%. The collection probability for the [1:1:0.2] ternary device is 77.7%. Ternary devices retained 99.4% of initial PCE after 1050 hours. Binary devices retained more than 97% of initial PCE after 1500 hours.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Higher coating temperatures induce better carrier collection. Temperatures above 100 °C cause edge aggregation, reducing FF. The 100 °C temperature minimizes bimolecular recombination. Trap-assisted recombination is the dominant mechanism in these devices. Adding PCBM creates an energy cascade effect. The ternary blend enhances exciton dissociation probability. The ternary blend improves charge collection probability. This work demonstrates the feasibility of roll-processed flexible OSCs.

Contradictions And Limitations
The devices were not prepared in a cleanroom or glovebox. This leads to high trap-assisted recombination. The efficiency gap between lab-scale and this work remains. The study uses a homemade roll-coater, not a full R2R line. The active area is small compared to industrial standards. The stability test was only under dark storage.

Claims
Slot-die coating of PM6:Y6 on flexible substrates is feasible using green solvents. The study demonstrates slot-die coating in open air. O-xylene was used as the green solvent. No additives were required for the process. The efficiency is lower than lab-scale spin-coated devices. This paves the way for upscaling OSC production.
Ternary blends with PCBM improve efficiency and stability. The champion efficiency reached 7.2%. Dissociation probability increased to 96.3%. Stability retained 99.4% after 1050 hours. The improvement in FF is modest. Ternary systems are promising for flexible OSCs.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study ablates coating temperature from 60 to 120 °C. The study ablates solution concentration from 12 to 28 mg/mL. The study compares binary and ternary blend ratios. Recombination mechanisms were analyzed via light intensity dependence.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the device structure and absorption spectra. Figure 2 shows J-V curves and EQE for different temperatures. Figure 3 shows box plots of PCE and FF vs temperature. Figure 4 shows images of the active layer stripe. Figure 5 shows box plots of PV parameters vs thickness. Figure 6 shows J-V curves and EQE for ternary devices. Figure 7 shows box plots comparing binary and ternary devices. Figure 8 shows stability data for binary and ternary devices. Table 1 lists PV parameters for different coating temperatures. Table 2 lists PV parameters for different AL thicknesses.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the demonstration of slot-die coated flexible PM6:Y6 OSCs. 2. The strongest evidence is the 7.2% efficiency and high stability. 3. The future path is upscaling to roll-to-roll manufacturing.
